title: How the World Added 20 Years of Life (1952–2007)

segments.narration: This is data on 142 countries from 1952 to 2007. In 1952, average life expectancy, weighted by population, was 48.9 years. By 2007 it was 68.9 years, a change of +20.0. So where did that change come from, and who got left behind?

params.title: Average life expectancy
params.source: Source: Gapminder Foundation (CC BY 4.0) · analysis: Compiled
params.label: population-weighted

claims.text: This is data on 142 countries from 1952 to 2007.
In 1952, average life expectancy, weighted by population, was 48.9 years.
By 2007 it was 68.9 years, a change of +20.0.

segments.narration: Split by continent, every continent's average was higher in 2007 than in 1952. Asia had the largest gain of any continent: from 42.9 years to 69.4 years. Meanwhile, Africa's average stayed between 53.3 and 53.4 from 1992 to 2002. For a decade, it barely moved.

claims.text: Split by continent, every continent's average was higher in 2007 than in 1952.

segments.narration: Put the first year next to the last, and the gaps tell a different story. The gap between Asia and Oceania went from 26.3 years to 11.7 years. But Africa was lowest at the start, at 38.8, and still lowest at the end, at 54.6.

params.title: 1952 vs 2007
params.source: Source: Gapminder Foundation (CC BY 4.0) · analysis: Compiled

claims.text: The gap between Asia and Oceania went from 26.3 years to 11.7 years.
But Africa was lowest at the start, at 38.8, and still lowest at the end, at 54.6.

segments.narration: Country by country, Oman gained the most: 38.1 years. Vietnam gained 33.8, and Indonesia 33.2. Not everyone moved forward. In Zimbabwe, life expectancy was 5.0 years lower in 2007 than in 1952.

params.title: Change in life expectancy, 1952–2007
params.source: Source: Gapminder Foundation (CC BY 4.0) · analysis: Compiled

claims.text: Country by country, Oman gained the most: 38.1 years.
In Zimbabwe, life expectancy was 5.0 years lower in 2007 than in 1952.

segments.narration: Each bubble is a country, sized by population, and they all drift up and to the right. In 2007, the correlation between log income per person and life expectancy was 0.81. In 1952, 5 of 142 countries were at 70 years or more; in 2007, 83 were. That link is strong, but a correlation alone can't tell us what causes what.
